title: What Is Shopify Catalog? How It Works and What It Means for Your Product Data
summary: Shopify Catalog is the product index AI agents search. See which products are included, what Shopify infers from your data and what you can control.
body_markdown:
Shopify Catalog is Shopify's index of products from eligible Shopify stores. AI agents and shopping apps search it to find and recommend products, and Shopify says it holds more than 1 billion products. Eligible products are included automatically, so most Shopify merchants are already in it.


What an agent finds there depends on your product data, and on what Shopify fills in when that data is thin. This guide covers how Shopify Catalog works, which products it includes, what Shopify adds to your data and what you can control.


## What is Shopify Catalog?


Shopify's help center describes Shopify Catalog as[a structured source of product information](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-catalog) gathered from eligible products sold by Shopify stores. Shopify[introduced it in May 2025](https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/introducing-shopify-catalog) for select partners building apps and AI agents. Developers can now search it through a[Catalog API](https://www.shopify.com/catalog) , which Shopify says covers more than 1 billion products from millions of merchants.


You don't send Shopify a feed for it. Products that meet Shopify's requirements are included by default, and Shopify keeps their price and stock tied to your store data.


### Which AI channels use Shopify Catalog


Shopify's agentic storefronts use the Catalog to sell in AI channels. Shopify's[agentic storefronts page](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/online-sales-channels/agentic-storefronts) names ChatGPT, Google AI Mode and Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, and Meta surfaces such as Muse.


The Shop app uses it too, and so do AI agents that connect through[Shopify Shop MCP](https://www.hypotenuse.ai/blog/shopify-shop-mcp) . Each channel decides which products to show and how to describe them.


## How does Shopify Catalog work?


Shopify structures the product data in your store and makes it searchable. An agent then searches the Catalog for products that match a shopper's request, or looks up a specific product to get its current price and stock. The agent decides how to rank and word what it finds.


### Which products are included


According to[Shopify's requirements](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-catalog/requirements) , a product is eligible when it:


- Has a title and at least one product image
- Has a price above zero
- Is published to your online store, Hydrogen or a headless channel, with a product URL
- Isn't unlisted or hidden from search engines
- Isn't in an excluded category


The store also needs to be on the Starter plan or higher and can't be in private mode. Excluded categories include alcohol, weapons, event tickets and product add-ons such as extended warranties. Products that Shopify classifies as Uncategorized are excluded too, so a product without a category doesn't reach any agent.


### What Shopify adds to your data


Shopify fills in details it can read from your data. Its[developer docs for the Catalog](https://shopify.dev/docs/agents/catalog/global-catalog) mark several fields as inferred, including the description agents see, product options, key features and attributes such as material, style and occasion. The docs say to treat these as "discovery and merchandising signals, not as merchant-authored source text."


Shopify also groups the same product sold by different stores under one Universal Product ID, so an agent can compare offers across merchants. When your own data is complete, Shopify has less to infer. When it's thin, the agent gets Shopify's reading of your product.


### Where shoppers check out


That depends on the channel. Shopify's help center says Microsoft Copilot, Meta surfaces, Google AI Mode and Gemini can use a Shopify-powered direct checkout inside the channel. ChatGPT sends shoppers to your online store to check out.


### What you can control


You can't opt out of Shopify Catalog itself. You can choose which AI channels get your products under Sales channels, then Agentic, in your Shopify admin. Turning a channel off leaves your products in the Catalog for uses like storefront search and the Shop app.


In the same section,[Shopify Catalog's product data mapping](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-catalog/mapping) lets you:


- Change which product field or metafield the Catalog uses for the title and description
- Choose price or compare-at price as the list price
- Group separate products into one listing with custom variant grouping


The product category can't be mapped, so the category set on the product is the one the Catalog uses. These settings work the same way as[Shopify channel mapping](https://www.hypotenuse.ai/blog/shopify-channel-mapping) for other channels: they change what the Catalog receives without changing your store data.


## Is Shopify Catalog the same as catalogs in Shopify Markets?


No. A catalog in Shopify Markets is a set of products, with optional custom pricing, that you assign to a market. It controls which products shoppers in that market can buy and at what price, as Shopify's[guide to catalogs for markets](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/markets/customizations/catalogs) explains.


Shopify Catalog is the product index that AI agents and shopping apps search. You don't create it or assign it to anything, and your eligible products are in it by default.


## How do you improve your products in Shopify Catalog?


Shopify's[guidance on optimizing products](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-catalog/optimizing-products) asks for accurate and detailed product information. It lists the fields AI platforms consider, including title, description, images, product type, tags, barcode and variant option names.


### Set the right category on every product


The category decides whether a product is in the Catalog at all, and it can't be mapped from another field. Use the most specific category that fits in Shopify's[product taxonomy](https://www.hypotenuse.ai/blog/ecommerce-product-taxonomy) .


### Write the facts shoppers ask about


Answer the questions shoppers ask before they buy, such as materials, dimensions, care and certifications, and put the key facts early in the description. Where your theme or filters use category metafields, fill those too, so Shopify reads the values instead of inferring them.


### Keep variants and barcodes clean


Name variant options plainly, such as Size and Color, and keep their values consistent across products. Add barcodes such as GTINs and UPCs, which Shopify lists among the fields AI platforms consider.


### Keep store policies current


Agents answer questions like "can I return this?" from the policies stored in Shopify. Shopify also offers a knowledge base in agentic storefronts for store information that isn't tied to one product.

## Frequently asked questions


### Do you need a product feed for Shopify Catalog?


No. Shopify builds the Catalog from the products already in your store, so there's nothing to upload. You choose which AI channels can use them in your Shopify admin.


### Does being in Shopify Catalog guarantee your products appear in ChatGPT?


No. Shopify says inclusion in the Catalog doesn't guarantee a product appears in a specific AI answer or ranks in a particular position. Each AI channel decides what to show.
